claim: A 6-rank host-staged all-reduce on a fast PCIe fabric (6x RTX 4090, NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1) reaches 1.45 GB/s algbw / 2.42 GB/s busbw at 64 MiB and an average busbw of 2.71 GB/s.
stance_target: cc-2's falsifier that a 5-rank no-P2P all-reduce could fall to <=0.1 GB/s algbw: a 6-rank host-staged run on a much faster fabric is 14-27x above that threshold
scope_conditions: 6x RTX 4090 on one node, mixed PHB/SYS topology, NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1, bf16 (half), all_reduce_perf -b 1M -e 64M -f 2 -g 6, 5 warmup / 20 iters, one process driving six GPUs
numbers: 64 MiB: 46,206 us, algbw 1.45 GB/s, busbw 2.42 GB/s

claim: NCCL maintainer sjeaugey attributes the low multi-GPU all-reduce bandwidth to CPU-side flow interleaving, not to the link: with 6 GPUs an all-reduce has 6 flows interleaving on the CPU, which breaks pipelining and can cost more than 2x.
stance_target: the reading that host-staged collectives at N>=5 are CPU/flow-contention bound, so the N=5 penalty is a software/topology artifact rather than a link-bandwidth collapse
quoted_support: That's unfortunately a common problem, in particular with AMD CPUs. Even though the p2pBandwidth benchmark shows 10GB/s (which is already not great), NCCL needs to communicate in both directions; it's not just a copy. This tends to decrease performance, even more than 2x. ... With 6 GPUs and an allreduce you have 6 flows interleaving on the CPU, which I'm not surprised leads to that performance.

claim: The reporter's all-pairs all_reduce_perf matrix on the same 6x4090 box shows pairwise busbw between 2.61 and 4.50 GB/s, i.e. even the best pair is only ~4.5 GB/s on a Gen4-class fabric.
stance_target: the ceiling of NCCL all-reduce on a PCIe-only fabric, which bounds any extrapolation to the 5-card box
scope_conditions: 6x RTX 4090, all ordered pairs, all_reduce_perf busbw
quoted_support: I measured the AllReduce bandwidth between every GPU pairs (all numbers are the bus bandwidth in GB/s from `all_reduce_perf`): | GPU0 | X | 2.61 | 3.60 | 3.58 | 3.57 | 3.59 ...

claim: The same box reports 'NCCL AllReduce can only achieve ~2.6 GB/s bus bandwidth while P2P test shows a much higher value', i.e. the collective is 4-5x slower than the raw peer copy rate.
stance_target: the efficiency factor between raw link rate and collective busbw, which is the key transfer parameter for extrapolating to Gen2 x4
scope_conditions: 6x RTX 4090, P2P disabled for the collective, p2pBandwidthLatencyTest for the raw copy
